examples.title: Minimal C Firmware & Portable Makefile
examples.verification_note: Verified against VEGA Studio's portable project scaffold (vega-project.json v1.0) and Make environment contract (CROSS_COMPILE, RISCV_ARCH=rv32i_zicsr, VEGA_MACHINE=THEJAS32). Hardware execution requires configuring a local VEGA SDK & target board.
examples.short_description: Clean freestanding C firmware entry point, app header, and portable Makefile wired to VEGA Studio build variables.
examples.long_description: Starts from a minimal, portable VEGA ARIES V3 firmware layout without hardcoding host paths. Demonstrates how VEGA Studio injects CROSS_COMPILE, RISCV_ARCH, and VEGA_MACHINE cleanly during Make builds.
examples.required_sdk: riscv32-vega-elf-gcc + GNU Make (or local VEGA SDK for board startup linking)
learning_objectives: Inspect freestanding C entry point without dynamic heap allocation
See how VEGA Studio passes CROSS_COMPILE, RISCV_ARCH, and VEGA_MACHINE
prerequisites: Optional: Phase 6 SDK Doctor configured for actual ELF compilation
examples.board_compatibility_note: Configured for VEGA_ARIES_V3 (VEGA ET1031, rv32i_zicsr, THEJAS32).

examples.title: RISC-V rv32i_zicsr CSR & Cycle Counter Patterns
examples.verification_note: Conceptual RISC-V ISA reference based on the ratified rv32i_zicsr specification (mcycle/mstatus CSR instructions). Check your local C-DAC VEGA SDK startup headers before enabling privileged CSR writes on hardware.
examples.short_description: Portable inline-assembly patterns for reading RISC-V Zicsr counters (mcycle/mstatus) with host-compile safety guards.
examples.long_description: Shows how the Zicsr ISA extension (explicitly configured in VEGA ARIES V3's target ISA `rv32i_zicsr`) provides atomic Control and Status Register reads/writes cleanly in embedded C.
examples.required_sdk: RISC-V 32-bit GCC with -march=rv32i_zicsr; SDK startup code for hardware execution
learning_objectives: Read 64-bit mcycle safely on a 32-bit RISC-V core (avoiding rollover tearing)
Use GCC constraints cleanly with csrr/csrs/csrc instructions
prerequisites: Basic C pointers and inline assembly syntax
examples.board_compatibility_note: Aligned with VEGA ARIES V3 ISA `rv32i_zicsr`. Board-specific machine CSRs beyond standard RISC-V require VEGA SDK documentation.

examples.title: 256 KB SRAM Static Memory & SPSC Ring Buffer
examples.verification_note: Conceptual firmware architecture pattern using standard C11/freestanding code sized appropriately for VEGA ARIES V3's verified 256 KB on-chip SRAM.
examples.short_description: Deterministic static allocation, _Static_assert budget guards, and a lock-free single-producer ring buffer without malloc.
examples.long_description: Bare-metal VEGA ARIES V3 firmware runs inside 256 KB SRAM shared across code/rodata, .data/.bss, and call stack. This example avoids heap fragmentation using compile-time bounded ring buffers and static capacity checks.
examples.required_sdk: Standard C toolchain; no external SDK peripherals required
learning_objectives: Implement a bounded single-producer/single-consumer ring buffer
Verify static buffer footprints with _Static_assert against SRAM limits
prerequisites: C arrays, structs, and bitwise masking
examples.board_compatibility_note: Respects VEGA_ARIES_V3 verified 256 KB on-chip SRAM ceiling.

examples.title: UART Telemetry Framing & Serial Parser
examples.verification_note: Conceptual framing & parser implementation; UART hardware initialization must be plugged in from your verified local VEGA SDK driver.
examples.short_description: Bounded line/frame telemetry state machine with XOR checksum verification built for USB-UART serial debugging.
examples.long_description: Demonstrates how to structure deterministic UART telemetry lines (`$VEGA,<seq>,<mv>*CS\r\n`) and parse incoming commands cleanly without buffer overruns before binding to VEGA ARIES V3 UART drivers.
examples.required_sdk: VEGA SDK UART RX/TX primitives required to run on USB-UART hardware
learning_objectives: Build bounded non-blocking UART line parsers
Compute NMEA-style XOR checksums for noisy serial links
Match CR/LF line endings configured in VEGA Studio Serial Monitor
examples.board_compatibility_note: Compatible conceptually with VEGA_ARIES_V3 CP210x/USB-UART workflows.

examples.title: ISR Flag Deferral & Event Queue Pattern
examples.verification_note: Conceptual interrupt design pattern. Exact ET1031 PLIC/CLINT IRQ numbers and VEGA SDK ISR registration macros are omitted until inspected in your local SDK.
examples.short_description: Keep interrupt service routines minimal: latch compact event flags cleanly and process heavy work in the main loop.
examples.long_description: Long loops or blocking serial writes inside ISRs cause missed ticks and latency spikes. This example separates fast interrupt capture (`volatile uint32_t`) from bounded main-loop dispatch.
examples.required_sdk: Local VEGA SDK interrupt/timer headers required to attach real hardware IRQs
learning_objectives: Minimize ISR execution time via deferred work flags
Protect shared state against compiler reordering with volatile
Recognize where verified SDK vector table/CSR setup hooks connect
prerequisites: C bitfields and main-loop superloop timing
examples.board_compatibility_note: Applies to bare-metal VEGA ET1031 single-core superloop firmware.

examples.title: MPU6050 IMU & BMP280 Barometer HAL Interface
examples.verification_note: Conceptual fixed-point sensor architecture for the verified onboard sensors (MPU6050 IMU, BMP280 Barometer) on VEGA ARIES V3. Register addresses/HAL callbacks must be supplied by your verified local VEGA SDK I2C driver.
examples.short_description: Clean hardware-independent C sensor abstraction injecting your VEGA SDK I2C read/write callbacks cleanly.
examples.long_description: Separates fixed-point IMU/barometer scaling and health state tracking from low-level I2C bus calls using a small vtable (`vega_i2c_bus_t`) ready to bind to verified VEGA SDK headers without hardcoding unverified registers.
examples.required_sdk: VEGA SDK I2C bus driver & verified sensor datasheet register definitions
learning_objectives: Decouple sensor logic from unverified board I2C driver signatures
Use integer scaling instead of linking software floating-point math on rv32i
Propagate deterministic I2C error codes safely
prerequisites: C structs, function pointers, fixed-point scaling
examples.board_compatibility_note: Matches VEGA_ARIES_V3 verified onboard sensors (MPU6050 IMU + BMP280 Barometer); no unverified I2C register constants fabricated.
